requirements.requirement: Run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker on node1 as a managed service named inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: The systemd unit was installed, enabled, and active with ExecStart pointing to the required worker. It was directly observed running before and after a node restart.

requirements.requirement: Run the service under the dedicated inventorysvc account.
requirements.summary: A dedicated non-login system account was created, the unit specifies that account and group, and the live post-restart process UID was verified as inventorysvc.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64 remained unchanged through configuration and restart. The existing worker and native systemd configuration executed successfully on that platform without package replacement or upgrade.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. inventory-worker is an enabled, active managed service running the required executable as inventorysvc, it recovered correctly after the mandatory node restart, and the installed RHEL release and kernel were preserved.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation and service installation were necessary task changes; the reboot scheduling was required by the provider-wide restart protocol. The remaining commands were read-only checks or bounded polling. After execution there were no failed services, new listening sockets, or package-health problems; the new systemd private temporary directory is expected service state. Restart evidence is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot scheduling, connection interruption, changed boot ID, and recovered enabled/active service with the correct process owner.
